claim: For the three-qubit Heisenberg \(XXX\) ring with one exchange impurity studied by Hu and Tian, let \(J_1>0\) be the two impurity-bond couplings, let \(J\) be the remaining bond coupling, and restrict to the zero-temperature-entangled regime \(r=J/J_1<1\). The impurity-neighbor concurrence has a unique positive critical temperature \(T_c\), and after setting \(u=J_1/T_c\) its threshold is the universal equation \[e^{6u}=e^{(2+4r)u}+4.\] Hence \(T_c/J_1=t(r)=1/u(r)\) is a single universal curve, with \(u(r)\) strictly increasing and \(t(r)\) strictly decreasing for all \(r<1\). As the antiferromagnetic activation boundary is approached, \(r\uparrow1\), \[\frac{T_c}{J_1}\sim\frac{6}{W\!\left(6/(1-r)\right)},\] where \(W\) is the principal Lambert function; equivalently, for fixed \(J>0\), \(T_c\sim 6J_1/W\!\left(6J_1/(J_1-J)\right)\) as \(J_1\downarrow J\). At the opposite strong-impurity endpoint, if \(z_0>1\) is the unique real root of \(z^3-z-4=0\), then \[T_c=\alpha J_1-\beta J+O(J^2/J_1),\qquad \alpha=\frac{2}{\log z_0}=3.414477321211954\ldots,\qquad \beta=\alpha\frac{z_0}{z_0+6}=0.786717182330735\ldots.\] The source reported only the numerical leading slope \(3.41448\) for \(J_1\gg |J|\); the universal scaling curve, its first finite-\(J\) correction, and the inverse-logarithmic collapse at \(J_1\downarrow J\) sharpen the impurity thermal-entanglement phase boundary.

correctness.rationale: The source formula gives \(C_{12}=\max\{0,(A-B-4C)/Z\}\). Its zero boundary is exactly \(e^{6u}=e^{(2+4r)u}+4\). Strict positivity of \(F_u\) for \(r<1\) proves uniqueness; implicit differentiation gives \(u\prime(r)>0\). The \(r\uparrow1\) balance yields \(6u\sim W(6/(1-r))\), and expansion at \(r=0\) yields the stated cubic constant and correction. Direct density-matrix replay agrees.
